chunks: Intelligence bears witness to that when it is freed from the shackles of desire, and safe from the attachments of this world.

key_terms.الْعَقْلُ: Intellect or reason, specifically the faculty of discernment in Shia thought
key_terms.الْهَوَى: Base desire or whims, often contrasted with intellect
key_terms.عَلاَئِقِ الدُّنْيَا: Attachments or fetters of the worldly life

ai.seo_question: What conditions must be met for the intellect to be considered sound and valid according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this letter to Malik al-Ashtar, Imam Ali establishes the epistemological foundation of just governance by linking intellectual clarity to spiritual purification. This aligns with the Shia concept of *al-'Aql* not merely as reason, but as the divine faculty that discerns truth when freed from the distractions of *al-Hawa* (base desires) and *ala'iq al-Dunya* (worldly ties), a theme resonating with the Quranic call to reflect and the purification of the soul.
